sanskrit: teṣu dharmānupūrvīṃ tāṃ prayujya madhusūdanaḥ yathāvayaḥ samīyāya rājabhis tatra mādhavaḥ
english: Having performed among them that proper greeting according to custom, Madhusūdana, the scion of Madhu, met with the kings there according to their respective seniority.

sanskrit: atha droṇaṃ saputraṃ sa bāhlīkaṃ ca yaśasvinam kṛpaṃ ca somadattaṃ ca samīyāya janārdanaḥ
english: Then Janārdana greeted Droṇa along with his son, and the glorious Bāhlīka, and Kṛpa, and Somadatta.

sanskrit: tatrāsīd ūrjitaṃ mṛṣṭaṃ kāñcanaṃ mahad āsanam śāsanād dhṛtarāṣṭrasya tatropāviśad acyutaḥ
english: There stood a grand, polished, golden seat of great magnificence; by the command of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, Acyuta sat upon it.

sanskrit: atha gāṃ madhuparkaṃ cāpy udakaṃ ca janārdane upajahrur yathānyāyaṃ dhṛtarāṣṭrapurohitāḥ
english: Then the priests of Dhṛtarāṣṭra duly offered Janārdana a cow, the honey-and-curd mixture (madhuparka), and water, as prescribed.

sanskrit: kṛtātithyas tu govindaḥ sarvān parihasan kurūn āste saṃbandhakaṃ kurvan kurubhiḥ parivāritaḥ
english: Govinda, having been received as a guest, sat cheerfully and conversationally, making friendly exchanges with all the Kurus, surrounded by them.

sanskrit: so 'rcito dhṛtarāṣṭreṇa pūjitaś ca mahāyaśāḥ rājānaṃ samanujñāpya nirākrāmad ariṃdamaḥ
english: Honored and worshipped by Dhṛtarāṣṭra, the greatly renowned subduer of foes then took leave of the king and departed.

sanskrit: taiḥ sametya yathānyāyaṃ kurubhiḥ kurusaṃsadi vidurāvasathaṃ ramyam upātiṣṭhata mādhavaḥ
english: Having duly met with the Kurus in the Kuru assembly, Mādhava then went to the pleasant residence of Vidura.

sanskrit: viduraḥ sarvakalyāṇair abhigamya janārdanam arcayām āsa dāśārhaṃ sarvakāmair upasthitam
english: Vidura approached Janārdana and honored the descendant of Dāśārha with all auspicious gifts and every comfort that was at hand.

sanskrit: kṛtātithyaṃ tu govindaṃ viduraḥ sarvadharmavit kuśalaṃ pāṇḍuputrāṇām apṛcchan madhusūdanam
english: Then Vidura, the knower of all dharma, having received Govinda as his guest, asked Madhusūdana about the welfare of the sons of Pāṇḍu.

sanskrit: prīyamāṇasya suhṛdo viduṣo buddhisattamaḥ dharmanityasya ca tadā gatadoṣasya dhīmataḥ
english: Of the pleased friend Vidura, the foremost in intelligence, ever firm in dharma, free of faults, and wise —

sanskrit: tasya sarvaṃ savistāraṃ pāṇḍavānāṃ viceṣṭitam kṣattur ācaṣṭa dāśārhaḥ sarvapratyakṣadarśivān
english: — to him the Dāśārha, who sees all things directly, narrated in full detail everything about the doings of the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca athopagamya viduram aparāhṇe janārdanaḥ pitṛṣvasāraṃ govindaḥ so 'bhyagacchad ariṃdamaḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then, in the afternoon, Janārdana went to Vidura and then Govinda, the subduer of foes, went to his father's sister (Kuntī).

sanskrit: sā dṛṣṭvā kṛṣṇam āyāntaṃ prasannādityavarcasam kaṇṭhe gṛhītvā prākrośat pṛthā pārthān anusmaran
english: She, upon seeing Kṛṣṇa coming with the serene radiance of the sun, took him by the neck and wept aloud, remembering the Pārthas.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ sattvavatāṃ madhye govindaṃ sahacāriṇam cirasya dṛṣṭvā vārṣṇeyaṃ bāṣpam āhārayat pṛthā
english: Among those men of valor, Pṛthā shed tears upon seeing, after a long time, the Vārṣṇeya Govinda, their companion.

sanskrit: sābravīt kṛṣṇam āsīnaṃ kṛtātithyaṃ yudhāṃ patim bāṣpagadgadapūrṇena mukhena pariśuṣyatā
english: She spoke to Kṛṣṇa, the lord of warriors, seated after being received as a guest, with a face full of choked sobs and dried by grief:

sanskrit: ye te bālyāt prabhṛtyeva guruśuśrūṣaṇe ratāḥ parasparasya suhṛdaḥ saṃmatāḥ samacetasaḥ
english: "Those who, from childhood on, were devoted to serving their elders, who were friends to one another, honored by all, and equal in spirit —

sanskrit: nikṛtyā bhraṃśitā rājyāj janārhā nirjanaṃ gatāḥ vinītakrodhaharṣāś ca brahmaṇyāḥ satyavādinaḥ
english: — those who deserved to be kings, deprived of their kingdom by treachery and gone to the wilderness, who had subdued anger and elation, who were devoted to the Brāhmaṇas and spoke the truth —

sanskrit: tyaktvā priyasukhe pārthā rudantīm apahāya mām ahārṣuś ca vanaṃ yāntaḥ samūlaṃ hṛdayaṃ mama
english: — the Pārthas, abandoning their beloved comforts, left me weeping and went to the forest, tearing my heart out by the root.

sanskrit: atadarhā mahātmānaḥ kathaṃ keśava pāṇḍavāḥ ūṣur mahāvane tāta siṃhavyāghragajākule
english: How, O Keśava, dear one, did those noble Pāṇḍavas, who did not deserve such a fate, dwell in the great forest teeming with lions, tigers, and elephants?

sanskrit: bālā vihīnāḥ pitrā te mayā satatalālitāḥ apaśyantaḥ svapitarau katham ūṣur mahāvane
english: Those boys, bereft of their father, ever pampered by me — how did they live in the great forest, unable to see their own parents?

sanskrit: śaṅkhadundubhinirghoṣair mṛdaṅgair vaiṇavair api pāṇḍavāḥ samabodhyanta bālyāt prabhṛti keśava
english: The Pāṇḍavas, O Keśava, used to be awakened from childhood by the sounds of conches and kettledrums, by mṛdaṅgas and flutes.

sanskrit: ye sma vāraṇaśabdena hayānāṃ heṣitena ca rathanemininādaiś ca vyabodhyanta sadā gṛhe
english: Those who were always awakened at home by the trumpeting of elephants, the neighing of horses, and the rumbling of chariot wheels —

sanskrit: śaṅkhabherīninādena veṇuvīṇānunādinā puṇyāhaghoṣamiśreṇa pūjyamānā dvijātibhiḥ
english: — honored by the twice-born with the blowing of conches and beating of kettledrums mingled with the sound of flutes and vīṇās and the chanting of auspicious recitations —

sanskrit: vastrai ratnair alaṃkāraiḥ pūjayanto dvijanmanaḥ gīrbhir maṅgalayuktābhir brāhmaṇānāṃ mahātmanām
english: — honoring the twice-born with garments, jewels, and ornaments, and with the auspicious songs of the great-souled Brāhmaṇas —

sanskrit: arcitair arcanārhaiś ca stuvadbhir abhinanditāḥ prāsādāgreṣv abodhyanta rāṅkavājinaśāyinaḥ
english: — worshipped by those worthy of worship and praised by those who praise, they used to awaken on the upper floors of palaces, sleeping on beds of soft deer-skin.

sanskrit: te nūnaṃ ninadaṃ śrutvā śvāpadānāṃ mahāvane na smopayānti nidrāṃ vai atadarhā janārdana
english: Those who do not deserve such a fate, upon hearing the howling of wild beasts in the great forest, surely could not fall asleep, O Janārdana.

sanskrit: bherīmṛdaṅganinadaiḥ śaṅkhavaiṇavanisvanaiḥ strīṇāṃ gītaninādaiś ca madhurair madhusūdana
english: By the sounds of kettledrums and mṛdaṅgas, by the notes of conches, flutes, and vīṇās, and by the sweet singing of women, O Madhusūdana —

sanskrit: bandimāgadhasūtaiś ca stuvadbhir bodhitāḥ katham mahāvane vyabodhyanta śvāpadānāṃ rutena te
english: — those who were awakened by bards, māgadhas, and sūtas singing praises, how could they be awakened in the great forest by the cries of wild beasts?

sanskrit: hrīmān satyadhṛtir dānto bhūtānām anukampitā kāmadveṣau vaśe kṛtvā satāṃ vartmānuvartate
english: He who is modest, firm in truth, self-controlled, compassionate to all beings, having conquered desire and hatred, follows the path of the righteous —

sanskrit: ambarīṣasya māndhātur yayāter nahuṣasya ca bharatasya dilīpasya śiber auśīnarasya ca
english: — the path of Ambarīṣa, Māndhātṛ, Yayāti, Nahuṣa, Bharata, Dilīpa, and Śibi the son of Uśīnara —

sanskrit: rājarṣīṇāṃ purāṇānāṃ dhuraṃ dhatte durudvahām śīlavṛttopasaṃpanno dharmajñaḥ satyasaṃgaraḥ
english: — the hard-to-bear yoke of the ancient royal sages he carries, endowed with good character and conduct, knowing dharma, and true to his vows.

sanskrit: rājā sarvaguṇopetas trailokyasyāpi yo bhavet ajātaśatrur dharmātmā śuddhajāmbūnadaprabhaḥ
english: He who would be fit to be king of all the three worlds, endowed with every virtue — Ajātaśatru, whose soul is dharma, with the pure lustre of refined gold —

sanskrit: śreṣṭhaḥ kuruṣu sarveṣu dharmataḥ śrutavṛttataḥ priyadarśano dīrghabhujaḥ kathaṃ kṛṣṇa yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: — foremost among all the Kurus in dharma, learning, and conduct, pleasing to behold, long-armed — how does Yudhiṣṭhira fare, O Kṛṣṇa?

sanskrit: yaḥ sa nāgāyutaprāṇo vātaraṃhā vṛkodaraḥ amarṣī pāṇḍavo nityaṃ priyo bhrātuḥ priyaṃkaraḥ
english: He whose vital force equals ten thousand elephants, who has the speed of the wind — Vṛkodara the Pāṇḍava, ever impatient, dear to his brother and ever doing what his brother loves —

sanskrit: kīcakasya ca sajñāter yo hantā madhusūdana śūraḥ krodhavaśānāṃ ca hiḍimbasya bakasya ca
english: — who was the slayer of Kīcaka and his kinsmen, O Madhusūdana, and the heroic slayer of those dominated by wrath — of Hiḍimba and Baka —

sanskrit: parākrame śakrasamo vāyuvegasamo jave maheśvarasamaḥ krodhe bhīmaḥ praharatāṃ varaḥ
english: — Bhīma, equal to Śakra in valor, equal to Vāyu in speed, equal to Maheśvara in wrath, the foremost of strikers —

sanskrit: krodhaṃ balam amarṣaṃ ca yo nidhāya paraṃtapaḥ jitātmā pāṇḍavo 'marṣī bhrātus tiṣṭhati śāsane
english: — he who, though the scorcher of enemies, having set aside his wrath, strength, and impatience, the self-mastered yet impatient Pāṇḍava, abides by his brother's command —

sanskrit: tejorāśiṃ mahātmānaṃ balaugham amitaujasam bhīmaṃ pradarśanenāpi bhīmasenaṃ janārdana taṃ mamācakṣva vārṣṇeya katham adya vṛkodaraḥ
english: — that great-souled mass of splendor, flood of strength, of immeasurable might, the fearsome Bhīmasena — O Janārdana, O Vārṣṇeya, tell me about him: how does Vṛkodara fare today?

sanskrit: āste parighabāhuḥ sa madhyamaḥ pāṇḍavo 'cyuta arjunenārjuno yaḥ sa kṛṣṇa bāhusahasriṇā dvibāhuḥ spardhate nityam atītenāpi keśava
english: That middle Pāṇḍava of club-like arms dwells there, O Acyuta. He who is Arjuna — O Kṛṣṇa — though having but two arms, always rivals Arjuna who has the strength of a thousand arms; and even the past, O Keśava.

sanskrit: kṣipaty ekena vegena pañca bāṇaśatāni yaḥ iṣvastre sadṛśo rājñaḥ kārtavīryasya pāṇḍavaḥ
english: He who with one stroke shoots five hundred arrows — that Pāṇḍava in archery is the equal of the king Kārtavīrya.

sanskrit: tejasādityasadṛśo maharṣipratimo dame kṣamayā pṛthivītulyo mahendrasamavikramaḥ
english: Resembling the sun in splendor, comparable to a great sage in self-restraint, equal to the earth in forbearance, and equal to Mahendra in valor —

sanskrit: ādhirājyaṃ mahad dīptaṃ prathitaṃ madhusūdana āhṛtaṃ yena vīryeṇa kurūṇāṃ sarvarājasu
english: — the great, blazing, celebrated sovereignty of the Kurus over all kings was won by whose valor, O Madhusūdana —

sanskrit: yasya bāhubalaṃ ghoraṃ kauravāḥ paryupāsate sa sarvarathināṃ śreṣṭhaḥ pāṇḍavaḥ satyavikramaḥ
english: — whose terrible strength of arm the Kauravas venerate — he, that Pāṇḍava of true valor, is the foremost of all chariot-warriors.

sanskrit: yo 'pāśrayaḥ pāṇḍavānāṃ devānām iva vāsavaḥ sa te bhrātā sakhā caiva katham adya dhanaṃjayaḥ
english: He who is the refuge of the Pāṇḍavas as Vāsava is of the gods — he is both your brother and friend — how does Dhanaṃjaya fare today?

sanskrit: dayāvān sarvabhūteṣu hrīniṣedho mahāstravit mṛduś ca sukumāraś ca dhārmikaś ca priyaś ca me
english: Compassionate to all beings, restrained by modesty, knowing great weapons, gentle, tender, righteous, and dear to me —

sanskrit: sahadevo maheṣvāsaḥ śūraḥ samitiśobhanaḥ bhrātṝṇāṃ kṛṣṇa śuśrūṣur dharmārthakuśalo yuvā
english: — Sahadeva, the great archer, heroic, glorious in battle, devoted in service to his brothers, O Kṛṣṇa, skilled in dharma and artha, and youthful —

sanskrit: sadaiva sahadevasya bhrātaro madhusūdana vṛttaṃ kalyāṇavṛttasya pūjayanti mahātmanaḥ
english: — the brothers of Sahadeva, O Madhusūdana, always honor the conduct of that great-souled one of auspicious conduct.

sanskrit: jyeṣṭhāpacāyinaṃ vīraṃ sahadevaṃ yudhāṃ patim śuśrūṣuṃ mama vārṣṇeya mādrīputraṃ pracakṣva me
english: O Vārṣṇeya, tell me of Sahadeva, that hero who reveres his eldest brother, lord of warriors, devoted in service, my Mādrī's son.

sanskrit: sukumāro yuvā śūro darśanīyaś ca pāṇḍavaḥ bhrātṝṇāṃ kṛṣṇa sarveṣāṃ priyaḥ prāṇo bahiścaraḥ
english: Tender, youthful, heroic, and handsome — that Pāṇḍava is dear to all his brothers, O Kṛṣṇa, the life-breath that roams outside them.

sanskrit: citrayodhī ca nakulo maheṣvāso mahābalaḥ kaccit sa kuśalī kṛṣṇa vatso mama sukhaidhitaḥ
english: Nakula, the versatile warrior, the great archer, of great strength — is he well, O Kṛṣṇa, that child of mine who was raised in comfort?

sanskrit: sukhocitam aduḥkhārhaṃ sukumāraṃ mahāratham api jātu mahābāho paśyeyaṃ nakulaṃ punaḥ
english: O great-armed one, shall I ever see Nakula again — he who is accustomed to ease, undeserving of sorrow, tender, and a great chariot-warrior?

sanskrit: pakṣmasaṃpātaje kāle nakulena vinākṛtā na labhāmi sukhaṃ vīra sādya jīvāmi paśya mām
english: Bereft of Nakula for the time it takes an eye to blink — even now I find no happiness, O hero; see how I merely survive.

sanskrit: sarvaiḥ putraiḥ priyatamā draupadī me janārdana kulīnā śīlasaṃpannā sarvaiḥ samuditā guṇaiḥ
english: Draupadī, most beloved by all my sons, O Janārdana, is of noble lineage, endowed with virtue, and complete in every quality.

sanskrit: putralokāt patilokān vṛṇvānā satyavādinī priyān putrān parityajya pāṇḍavān anvapadyata
english: That truth-speaking one, choosing the world of her husbands over the world of her sons, abandoned her beloved children and followed the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: mahābhijanasaṃpannā sarvakāmaiḥ supūjitā īśvarī sarvakalyāṇī draupadī katham acyuta
english: Born of great lineage, well-honored with every comfort, mistress of all blessings — how does Draupadī fare, O Acyuta?

sanskrit: patibhiḥ pañcabhiḥ śūrair agnikalpaiḥ prahāribhiḥ upapannā maheṣvāsair draupadī duḥkhabhāginī
english: Draupadī, attended by five heroic husbands like fires, strikers of blows, great archers — she has become a sharer in suffering.

sanskrit: caturdaśam imaṃ varṣaṃ yan nāpaśyam ariṃdama putrādhibhiḥ paridyūnāṃ draupadīṃ satyavādinīm
english: This is the fourteenth year that I have not seen Draupadī, O subduer of foes — the truth-speaking one worn down by anguish over her sons.

sanskrit: na nūnaṃ karmabhiḥ puṇyair aśnute puruṣaḥ sukham draupadī cet tathāvṛttā nāśnute sukham avyayam
english: Surely a person does not attain happiness through meritorious deeds, if Draupadī, who has conducted herself thus, does not enjoy imperishable happiness.

sanskrit: na priyo mama kṛṣṇāya bībhatsur na yudhiṣṭhiraḥ bhīmaseno yamau vāpi yad apaśyaṃ sabhāgatām
english: Neither Bībhatsu nor Yudhiṣṭhira nor Bhīmasena nor the twins was dear to me when I saw Kṛṣṇā (Draupadī) dragged into the assembly.

sanskrit: na me duḥkhataraṃ kiṃ cid bhūtapūrvaṃ tato 'dhikam yad draupadīṃ nivātasthāṃ śvaśurāṇāṃ samīpagām
english: Nothing has ever been more painful to me than seeing Draupadī, who had sought shelter with her elders-in-law, who had gone near her fathers-in-law —

sanskrit: ānāyitām anāryeṇa krodhalobhānuvartinā sarve praikṣanta kurava ekavastrāṃ sabhāgatām
english: — dragged in by that ignoble one who followed anger and greed, while all the Kurus watched her, clad in a single garment, brought into the assembly.

sanskrit: tatraiva dhṛtarāṣṭraś ca mahārājaś ca bāhlikaḥ kṛpaś ca somadattaś ca nirviṇṇāḥ kuravas tathā
english: There too were Dhṛtarāṣṭra, the great king Bāhlika, Kṛpa, Somadatta, and likewise the Kurus — all overcome with shame.

sanskrit: tasyāṃ saṃsadi sarvasyāṃ kṣattāraṃ pūjayāmy aham vṛttena hi bhavaty āryo na dhanena na vidyayā
english: In that entire assembly, I honor the Kṣattṛ (Vidura); for one becomes noble by conduct, not by wealth, not by learning.

sanskrit: tasya kṛṣṇa mahābuddher gambhīrasya mahātmanaḥ kṣattuḥ śīlam alaṃkāro lokān viṣṭabhya tiṣṭhati
english: O Kṛṣṇa, the character of that Kṣattṛ — of great intellect, profound, and great-souled — stands as an ornament pervading all the worlds.

sanskrit: sā śokārtā ca hṛṣṭā ca dṛṣṭvā govindam āgatam nānāvidhāni duḥkhāni sarvāṇy evānvakīrtayat
english: She, both grieving and rejoiced upon seeing Govinda arrived, recounted all the sorrows of every kind she had endured.

sanskrit: pūrvair ācaritaṃ yat tat kurājabhir ariṃdama akṣadyūtaṃ mṛgavadhaḥ kaccid eṣāṃ sukhāvaham
english: "That which was practiced by wicked kings of old, O subduer of foes — the dice game and the hunting of deer — has it brought happiness to these?"

sanskrit: tan māṃ dahati yat kṛṣṇā sabhāyāṃ kurusaṃnidhau dhārtarāṣṭraiḥ parikliṣṭā yathā nakuśalaṃ tathā
english: This burns me — that Kṛṣṇā (Draupadī), in the assembly in the presence of the Kurus, was tormented by the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra as if it were no harm at all.

sanskrit: nirvāsanaṃ ca nagarāt pravrajyā ca paraṃtapa nānāvidhānāṃ duḥkhānām āvāso 'smi janārdana ajñātacaryā bālānām avarodhaś ca keśava
english: The banishment from the city, the exile, O scorcher of foes — I am a dwelling-place of manifold sorrows, O Janārdana; the period of incognito life, and the confinement of the young ones, O Keśava.

sanskrit: na sma kleśatamaṃ me syāt putraiḥ saha paraṃtapa duryodhanena nikṛtā varṣam adya caturdaśam
english: No affliction would be too great for me if I were with my sons, O scorcher of enemies — yet I have been deceived by Duryodhana for now fourteen years.

sanskrit: duḥkhād api sukhaṃ na syād yadi puṇyaphalakṣayaḥ na me viśeṣo jātv āsīd dhārtarāṣṭreṣu pāṇḍavaiḥ
english: If meritorious deeds bear no fruit, even happiness would not arise from suffering. I never made any distinction between the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra and the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: tena satyena kṛṣṇa tvāṃ hatāmitraṃ śriyā vṛtam asmād vimuktaṃ saṃgrāmāt paśyeyaṃ pāṇḍavaiḥ saha naiva śakyāḥ parājetuṃ sattvaṃ hy eṣāṃ tathāgatam
english: By that truth, O Kṛṣṇa, may I see you, the slayer of enemies, adorned with glory, freed from this battle — together with the Pāṇḍavas. They cannot be defeated, for their innate nature is such.

sanskrit: pitaraṃ tv eva garheyaṃ nātmānaṃ na suyodhanam yenāhaṃ kuntibhojāya dhanaṃ dhūrtair ivārpitā
english: I would blame only my father, not myself, not Suyodhana — by whom I was given to Kuntibhoja like goods handed over by gamblers.

sanskrit: bālāṃ mām āryakas tubhyaṃ krīḍantīṃ kanduhastakām adadāt kuntibhojāya sakhā sakhye mahātmane
english: My grandfather gave me, a little girl playing with a ball in my hands, to Kuntibhoja as a friend gives to a friend — the great-souled one to one like him.

sanskrit: sāhaṃ pitrā ca nikṛtā śvaśuraiś ca paraṃtapa atyantaduḥkhitā kṛṣṇa kiṃ jīvitaphalaṃ mama
english: I, thus deceived by my father and by my fathers-in-law, O scorcher of enemies, in extreme grief — O Kṛṣṇa, what is the fruit of my life?

sanskrit: yan mā vāg abravīn naktaṃ sūtake savyasācinaḥ putras te pṛthivīṃ jetā yaśaś cāsya divaṃ spṛśet
english: The voice that spoke to me at night at the birth of Savyasāci: 'Your son will conquer the earth and his fame will touch the heavens' —

sanskrit: hatvā kurūn grāmajanye rājyaṃ prāpya dhanaṃjayaḥ bhrātṛbhiḥ saha kaunteyas trīn medhān āhariṣyati
english: — 'Having slain the Kurus in the village battle, Dhanaṃjaya, the son of Kuntī, will obtain the kingdom together with his brothers and perform three great sacrifices' —

sanskrit: nāhaṃ tām abhyasūyāmi namo dharmāya vedhase kṛṣṇāya mahate nityaṃ dharmo dhārayati prajāḥ
english: I do not resent that voice. Homage to dharma, to the Creator, to the great Kṛṣṇa (the dark one); eternally dharma upholds all creatures.

sanskrit: dharmaś ced asti vārṣṇeya tathā satyaṃ bhaviṣyati tvaṃ cāpi tat tathā kṛṣṇa sarvaṃ saṃpādayiṣyasi
english: If dharma exists, O Vārṣṇeya, then truth will prevail; and you, O Kṛṣṇa, will also bring all that to fulfillment.

sanskrit: na māṃ mādhava vaidhavyaṃ nārthanāśo na vairitā tathā śokāya bhavati yathā putrair vinābhavaḥ
english: O Mādhava, widowhood does not grieve me, nor the loss of wealth, nor enmity — nothing grieves me as much as being separated from my sons.

sanskrit: yāhaṃ gāṇḍīvadhanvānaṃ sarvaśastrabhṛtāṃ varam dhanaṃjayaṃ na paśyāmi kā śāntir hṛdayasya me
english: I who do not see Dhanaṃjaya, the Gāṇḍīva-bowman, the foremost among all bearers of weapons — what peace can there be for my heart?
